description: Quota, tokens and API cost for Claude Code and Codex, permanently in the status bar — coloured by pace, not by level.
capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces: Token Pace never reads, executes or evaluates workspace content. It reads Claude Code's and Codex's transcript files in your home directory and writes only into its own extension storage. The two exceptions — writing the external quota cache file and installing the Claude status-line bridge — are opt-in, each behind its own consent dialog, and both are disabled in Restricted Mode.
capabilities.virtualWorkspaces: Token Pace does not read the workspace at all, so it works in virtual workspaces. Its data comes from local files in your home directory; on a virtual or remote workspace without those files it reports that it found none instead of showing zeros.

configuration.general.title: General
config.statusBar.show.description:
Which entries the status bar shows — **and in which order**: the array order is the display order (drag the rows in the settings UI). The order *inside* one entry is fixed.

An empty list hides the status bar entirely. Use `#tokenPace.windowSelect#` to control how many quota windows each tool contributes and `#tokenPace.density#` to control how much text each one gets.
config.statusBar.show.enum.extra: Extra/purchased usage on top of the plan
config.statusBar.show.enum.context: Context window of the current Claude Code session, e.g. “ctx 42%” — needs the connected status line
config.statusBar.show.enum.tokens: Tokens used in the summary period
config.statusBar.show.enum.cost: Hypothetical API cost for the summary period — needs tokenPace.showCost
config.statusBar.show.enum.forecast: Burn-rate forecast, e.g. “~empty in 40 min” — needs tokenPace.quotaHistoryDays above 0
config.statusBar.show.enum.budget: The budget closest to its own limit, e.g. “budget 63 %” — needs tokenPace.budgets
config.windowSelect.description:
Which quota windows appear in the status bar. The default `worstPace` gives each tool **one** entry: the window that needs attention — the worst pace verdict, and within one verdict the most-utilised of those windows.

`all` puts every window in the bar and can produce up to nine entries. The command *Token Pace: Cycle Status Bar Windows* steps through these values without opening the settings.
config.windowSelect.enum.all: Every window as its own entry, including model-scoped ones — “CC 5h 25%”, “CC 7d 69%”, “CC Fable 7d 12%”
config.windowSelect.enum.leading: Only the most-utilised window per tool — “CC 7d 69%”
config.windowSelect.enum.worstPace: Only the window with the worst pace verdict; within one verdict the most-utilised of them — “CC 5h 25% ▲”
config.windowSelect.enum.auto: Session window; the weekly window is added once the session window is below 30 % — “CC 5h 12% | 7d 69%”
config.density.description:
How much text each status bar entry gets.

In non-data states (no token, offline, consent pending) and in the alarm state the icon and the window label stay visible at every density — a compact bar never hides *why* there is no number.

Use *Token Pace: Preview Status Bar States* to see all states side by side before you decide.
config.density.enum.compact: One item per tool, coloured by its worst window — “CC 25%·2h14m | 69%·6d”
config.density.enum.minimal: One item in total, coloured by the worst window of all — “TP 25% ▲”
config.clickAction.description:
What a click on a status bar entry does. The default opens the dashboard; `menu` opens the Quick Pick with every action instead.

In a problem state the click always performs the repair step instead — consent dialog, forced fetch, or the relevant setting.
config.clickAction.enum.menu: Open a Quick Pick with dashboard, text view, fetch, re-read, log and settings
config.clickAction.enum.refresh: Fetch the quota now (respects the backoff)
config.clickAction.enum.openWebsite: Open the provider's official usage page in the browser
config.usagePageLinks.description:
Make the tooltip title a link to the provider's official usage page (`https://claude.ai/settings/usage`, `https://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/usage`) and offer *Open Official Usage Page* in the menu.

The extension itself never contacts those pages; the link opens in your browser.
config.alignment.description: Right-aligned entries are hidden **without notice** when the window is narrow. `left` is recommended.
config.alignment.enum.left: Left half of the status bar — recommended
config.alignment.enum.right: Right half of the status bar
config.staleAfterMinutes.description: Age from which a quota reading counts as stale: it is greyed out with `tokenPace.stale`, marked in the tooltip, and no alert may fire from it.
config.timezone.description:
Which zone day and hour boundaries use: `system`, `utc`, or an IANA name such as `Europe/Berlin`. It governs the status bar summary as well as the dashboard.

An unusable value falls back to the system zone. This is a display decision only — nothing is re-counted.
config.dayBoundaryHour.description: The hour at which a “day” starts, for the status bar summary as well as the dashboard. `4` books work between midnight and 04:00 onto the previous day. Display only.
config.planName.description:
Plan name shown beside the provider title (Pro, Max 20x, Team).

```json
"tokenPace.planName": { "claude": "Max 20x", "codex": "Plus" }
```

Display only — Token Pace never derives a limit, a window or a denominator from it. A name a provider states itself always wins; yours is printed as `plan Max 20x (as configured)` so the two can be told apart. Values over 40 characters are cut.
config.planName.claude.description: Plan name shown beside the Claude Code title, e.g. "Max 20x".
config.planName.codex.description: Plan name shown beside the Codex title, e.g. "Plus".
config.keybindings.description:
Bind `ctrl+alt+shift+t` (`cmd+alt+shift+t` on macOS) to *Token Pace: Open Dashboard*.

Turn it off to free the chord without writing a `-` rule into `keybindings.json`. Every command stays available from the Command Palette either way; Token Pace claims no other shortcut.
config.windows.description: **Deprecated** — use `#tokenPace.windowSelect#`. Still read while `#tokenPace.windowSelect#` is at its default (`worstPace`), so an existing `leading` keeps working; setting `#tokenPace.windowSelect#` to anything else overrides it.
config.windows.deprecation: Replaced by tokenPace.windowSelect, which has four more values. This setting is still honoured while tokenPace.windowSelect is at its default.
config.windows.enum.all: Every quota window as its own entry
config.windows.enum.leading: Only the most-utilised window per tool
configuration.pace.title: Pace
config.pace.sensitivity.description:
How far ahead of pace a window may run before Token Pace colours it.

The verdict compares consumption with elapsed time:

`ratio = (used ÷ limit) ÷ (elapsed ÷ window)`

`1.0` is exactly on pace, above `1.0` means you are consuming faster than the window refills. Token Pace states the same relation in percentage points (`used % − elapsed %`), because that number stays meaningful near the start and the end of a window; the tolerance below is measured in those points.

Presets (tolerance points / minimum elapsed): `relaxed` 10 / 5 (≈ ratio 1.2), `normal` 5 / 3 (≈ ratio 1.12), `strict` 2 / 1 (≈ ratio 1.05). `custom` unlocks the two settings below.
config.pace.sensitivity.enum.relaxed: 10 tolerance points, 5 % minimum elapsed — roughly ratio 1.2 at the window mid-point
config.pace.sensitivity.enum.normal: 5 tolerance points, 3 % minimum elapsed — roughly ratio 1.12
config.pace.sensitivity.enum.strict: 2 tolerance points, 1 % minimum elapsed — roughly ratio 1.05
config.pace.tolerancePoints.description:
Only used with `#tokenPace.pace.sensitivity#` set to `custom`.

Dead band in **percentage points** between consumption and elapsed time before a window is coloured as ahead of pace — with `ratio = (used ÷ limit) ÷ (elapsed ÷ window)`, 5 points at the window mid-point is about `ratio 1.12`. The exact difference is always in the tooltip, tolerance or not.
config.pace.minElapsedPercent.descriptio:
Only used with `#tokenPace.pace.sensitivity#` set to `custom`.

How much of a window must have elapsed before a small reading is judged. Right after a reset `elapsed ≈ 0`, so `ratio = (used ÷ limit) ÷ (elapsed ÷ window)` explodes and the very first prompt would always look “too fast”. Below this value, and while at most twice the tolerance of the window is used, the verdict reads “measuring (window just reset)”; a larger reading is judged from the first minute.
config.pace.levels.description: How many warning levels the pace verdict has. The exhausted state (≥ 99.5 %) always wins over both.
config.pace.levels.enum.binary: On pace or ahead — one warning level
config.pace.levels.enum.graded: A second level beyond three times the tolerance, shown as “▲▲” and tokenPace.paceAhead
configuration.statusBarLook.title: Status bar
config.barWidth.description: Bar width in characters. `0` hides the bars and leaves the percentage. The time marker needs at least 6.
config.barStyle.description:
Only applies to `#tokenPace.barGlyphs#` `blocks`: `line` and `shade` differ only there.

How the **empty** part of the bar is drawn. The `shapes` and `dots` sets bring their own empty glyph (`□`, `○`) so the bar stays inside one Unicode block, and `pie` has no empty part at all — for those three only `none` changes anything.
config.barStyle.enum.line: Thin baseline as the track — “██▁▁▁▁▁▁”, quiet, recommended
config.barStyle.enum.shade: Dotted shading as the track — “██░░░░░░”, more contrast, grainy at small font sizes
config.barStyle.enum.none: No track, only the filled part — “██”
config.barGlyphs.description: Which glyph set draws the bar. Which of these looks right depends entirely on your status bar font — Token Pace cannot measure that, so all four are offered.
config.barGlyphs.enum.shapes: Squares — “■■□□□□□□”, recommended on Windows, where eighth blocks often render unevenly
config.barGlyphs.enum.pie: A single pie glyph — “◑”, ignores tokenPace.barWidth
config.timeProgressStyle.description: How elapsed time is shown in the bar. This is what makes pace readable **without colour**: consumption left of the marker means reserve, right of it means ahead of pace.
config.timeProgressStyle.enum.marker: A marker inside the bar at the elapsed position — “██▁┃▁▁▁▁” (needs tokenPace.barWidth ≥ 6)
config.timeProgressStyle.enum.bar: A second, thinner bar for elapsed time — “██▁▁▁▁▁▁ ▔▔▔▁▁▁▁▁”
config.timeProgressStyle.enum.none: No time indication in the bar
config.indicator.description: How the pace verdict is signalled. Colour alone is invisible to red-green colour blind readers and disappears in themes that tint the whole status bar.
config.indicator.enum.glyph: Glyph only — “CC 5h 25% ▲” ahead, “▲▲” far ahead, “!” exhausted
config.indicator.enum.both: Colour and glyph — readable with red-green colour blindness and in coloured status bars
config.colorMode.description: The four colours are contributed theme colours: override them in `workbench.colorCustomizations` under `tokenPace.paceOk`, `tokenPace.paceWarn`, `tokenPace.paceAhead` and `tokenPace.stale`.
config.colorMode.enum.theme: Use the theme colours tokenPace.paceOk / paceWarn / paceAhead / stale
config.colorMode.enum.monochrome: No colour at all — glyphs only
config.percentMode.description: Whether the number is what you used or what is left. The choice is carried through item, bar direction, tooltip and legend consistently.
config.percentMode.enum.remaining: Share left — “75%”, bar fills the other way, like a battery
config.resetFormat.description:
Countdown suffix behind the percentage, used identically in item, tooltip and dashboard.

A window whose provider states no reset time gets **no** countdown — never an invented one. A reset that has passed without a fresh reading reads “reset due”, never a negative number.
config.resetFormat.enum.absolute: Clock time, with the weekday beyond 24 h — “CC 5h 25% · 06:00”, “· Mo 06:00”
config.showAgeInItem.description: Show how old the quota reading is inside the status bar entry. The age is recomputed against the clock at every redraw, so it never freezes at the value it had when it was fetched.
config.showAgeInItem.enum.never: Never — the tooltip still names the age
config.labels.description:
Custom prefixes and window labels. Keys are either a tool prefix (`claude`, `codex`) or a stable window id: Claude `session:300`, `weekly_all:10080`, `weekly_scoped:10080:<model>` (e.g. `weekly_scoped:10080:fable`); Codex `<limitId>:<minutes>` (e.g. `codex:10080`, `codex:300`). The ids are listed in docs/status-bar-states.md and in **Token Pace: Copy Diagnostics**. Values longer than 40 characters are cut.

```json
"tokenPace.labels": {
  "claude": "CC",
  "weekly_all:10080": "week"
}
```
config.summary.period.description: Which period the token and cost entries sum up. Anything but `today` is named in the entry text so the number is never ambiguous.
config.summary.scope.description: Which tools the token and cost entries sum up.
config.tooltip.description: How much the status bar tooltip shows.
config.tooltip.enum.full: Table, explanations, forecast, provenance line and action links
config.tooltip.enum.compact: Table and action links only, at most 12 lines — “Window | Used | Elapsed | Pace | Resets”
config.tooltipExplanations.description:
Show the explanatory paragraphs in the tooltip (what pace means, what the cost figure is and is not). **Off by default** — they are worth reading once, not on every hover.

Uncertainty markers (`~`, `⚠`) and the provenance line are never hidden by this setting.
config.overflowDisplay.description: What to do when a provider reports more than 100 % (extra usage or purchased credits on top of the plan).
config.overflowDisplay.enum.actual: Show the real value including paid overflow — “111%”
config.resetHourCycle.description: Clock format for absolute reset times.
config.labelMaxChars.description: Truncate generated window labels to this many characters. `0` means no truncation.
configuration.dashboard.title: Dashboard
config.dashboard.sections.description:
Which sections the **Token Pace** panel shows — **and in which order**: the array order is the render order.

`projects` and `sessions` stay empty until `#tokenPace.attribution#` is switched on.
config.dashboard.sections.enum.summary: Rule-based summary sentences, each with its number and basis
config.dashboard.sections.enum.quota: Quota cards with bar, elapsed tick, verdict and reset
config.dashboard.sections.enum.context: Context window of the current Claude Code session, as the status line reported it — needs the connected status line
config.dashboard.sections.enum.kpis: KPI row: today, usage, cost, requests, cache hit, active days, avg per active day
config.dashboard.sections.enum.tokens: Token totals with fresh input, cache write 5m/1h, cache read, output, reasoning
config.dashboard.sections.enum.chart: Stacked daily chart of the selected range
config.dashboard.sections.enum.models: Breakdown by model with cost, cache hit rate and share
config.dashboard.sections.enum.heatmap: Calendar heatmap of the last 53 weeks
config.dashboard.sections.enum.records: Records of the selected range: peak day, longest streak with usage, and the top models, projects and sessions
config.dashboard.sections.enum.tools: Tool calls by name, with the share of the calls counted in the range and the models that made them
config.dashboard.sections.enum.budget: Your own budgets from tokenPace.budgets: used, limit, share and the end-of-period projection
config.dashboard.sections.enum.history: Reset retrospective: peak per cycle, unused at reset, capped share — needs tokenPace.quotaHistoryDays above 0
config.dashboard.sections.enum.sessions: Per-session breakdown (needs tokenPace.attribution set to session)
config.dashboard.sections.enum.dataQuali: Data quality: roots, file counts, retention, quota origins, drift
config.dashboard.defaultRange.descriptio: The range the dashboard opens with. Ranges you pick in the panel are remembered for the session; this is the starting point.
config.dashboard.defaultRange.enum.thisW: The current week, starting at tokenPace.startOfWeek
config.dashboard.modelRows.description: How many rows the model table shows before the rest is folded into a “… n more” line. `0` shows every model.
config.dashboard.topN.description:
How many rows each table of the `records` and `tools` sections of `#tokenPace.dashboard.sections#` shows — top models, projects, sessions and tools.

A cap on what is *listed*, never on what is counted: the shares beside the rows are shares of everything in the range.
config.dashboard.mode.description: What *Open Dashboard* and a click on the status bar open. All three read the same view model, so the numbers cannot drift apart.
config.dashboard.mode.enum.webview: Full panel in the secondary side bar — charts, heatmap, drilldown
config.dashboard.mode.enum.quickPick: A Quick Pick list — keyboard-first, no webview, same numbers
config.dashboard.mode.enum.markdown: A read-only Markdown document with tables and ASCII bars — copyable
config.startOfWeek.description: First day of the week for the heatmap, the weekday grid and the `thisWeek` range.
config.planPriceUsd.description:
What you pay per month, per tool. Only used for one derived line — how many times over the hypothetical API cost exceeds the subscription price.

```json
"tokenPace.planPriceUsd": { "claude": 100, "codex": 20 }
```

Leave it empty and the line is simply not shown; Token Pace never guesses a plan price.
config.planPriceUsd.claude.description: Monthly price of your Claude plan in USD.
config.planPriceUsd.codex.description: Monthly price of your ChatGPT/Codex plan in USD.
config.calibration.show.description:
Show how many local tokens correspond to one percentage point of a quota window, derived from your own history.

This is an observation about your data, not a published limit — the providers do not document the conversion, and it changes with model and cache mix. Off by default because it invites over-interpretation.
configuration.cost.title: Cost
config.showCost.description:
Show the **API cost** column: what this usage would have cost through the provider API at list prices.

This is a hypothetical figure. On a subscription you do **not** pay these amounts — there is no billing relationship. Every such number is marked with `~`.

With this off, the `cost` entry of `#tokenPace.statusBar.show#` is not created either.
config.customPrices.item.cacheWrite5m.de: USD per 1M tokens written to the 5-minute cache.
config.customPrices.item.cacheWrite1h.de: USD per 1M tokens written to the 1-hour cache.
config.customPrices.item.fast.descriptio: Fast-mode rates, USD per 1M tokens. Both fields are required. Without a fast rate, fast-mode requests stay unpriced (marked ⚠) instead of being priced at the standard rate.
config.pricing.multiplier.description: Factor applied to every list price, for contract discounts — `0.9` for 10 % off. Any value other than `1` marks the figures as “at your configured rates”.
config.unknownModelPricing.description: What to do with a model that is not in the price table. `strict` reports a lower bound instead of inventing a number; `family` gives an estimate and says so.
config.unknownModelPricing.enum.strict: A model without a price stays unpriced and is named as such
config.unknownModelPricing.enum.family: Fall back to the newest priced model of the same family, marked “family price”
config.budgets.description:
Limits **you** state, measured against the locally counted usage.

```json
"tokenPace.budgets": [
  { "scope": "total", "period": "month", "unit": "usd", "limit": 200 },
  { "scope": "claude", "period": "day", "unit": "tokens", "limit": 5000000 }
]
```

**`usd` is the hypothetical API equivalent, not a bill** — on a subscription you do not pay these amounts, and unpriced models make the figure a lower bound (marked ⚠). A budget is never a quota: nothing here is derived from a plan, and a period with no local data shows a dash rather than 0 %.

Show them with the `budget` section of `#tokenPace.dashboard.sections#`; an entry with an unknown scope, period or unit is dropped whole rather than repaired. At most 20 budgets, one per scope × period × unit.
config.budgets.period.description: The period it is measured over, in your own zone and week.
config.budgets.unit.description: usd = the hypothetical API equivalent, not a bill. tokens = billable tokens.
config.budgets.limit.description: Your own number. An entry without a finite limit above zero is dropped whole.
config.budgets.label.description: Optional name shown instead of "All providers · this month".
config.pricing.showListPrice.description: Show the undiscounted list price as a second column next to your own rates, in the manner of the `amount` / `list_amount` pair of the provider analytics APIs.
configuration.quotaSources.title: Quota sources
config.quotaSource.description:
Where the quota figures come from. Token counts come from local transcript files either way and never need network access.

**The trade-off:** local sources (cache file, Claude status line, **~/.claude.json**, Codex transcripts) cost nothing, need no credentials and touch no network — but they are as old as the last time something else wrote them, which can be hours. Fetching gets the current number from the provider, at the price of a network request with your access token and an undocumented endpoint that may change without notice.

`auto` (default) reads only local sources and **makes no network access of its own**. If none of them has data, it offers once to switch to `poll`.

`poll` fetches directly: the access token from `~/.claude/.credentials.json` goes to `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage`, and the local `codex app-server` is started. This happens only after you have explicitly agreed in a dialog that states exactly what is sent. The token is only **read**, **never refreshed**, never logged, never put in an error message or in the diagnostics, and never sent anywhere else.

`cache` settles the question for good: local sources only, no offer.
config.quotaSource.enum.auto: Local sources only; offer once to fetch if none of them has data — recommended
config.quotaSource.enum.poll: Fetch from the provider as well — requires your one-time consent
config.quotaSource.enum.cache: Local sources only, never fetch and never ask
config.pollIntervalMinutes.description: Interval between the extension's own fetches, in minutes. Only applies where fetching actually happens (see `#tokenPace.quotaSource#`). Failures trigger a growing backoff (429: up to 2 h, network: up to 30 min), and the consent dialog names the value you set here.
config.claudeQuotaSources.description:
Which Claude sources may be used, in order of preference on a tie. The **freshest** source that has data wins; the order only breaks ties, so a stale preferred source never hides a current one.

Fields are never merged across sources — a reading always comes from one identity.
config.claudeQuotaSources.enum.cacheFile: The external cache file written by a poller of your choice — see tokenPace.claudeQuotaFile
config.claudeQuotaSources.enum.statuslin: The mirror file of the Claude status-line bridge, if you installed it
config.claudeQuotaSources.enum.claudeJso: The cachedUsageUtilization object in ~/.claude.json, written by Claude Code itself
config.claudeQuotaSources.enum.poll: Token Pace's own network fetch — only with tokenPace.quotaSource set to poll and after consent
config.codexQuotaSources.description:
Which Codex sources may be used, in order of preference on a tie. The freshest source with data wins.

`transcript` is free: those lines already pass through the token parser. Since some Codex builds write `rate_limits: null`, its age is always shown.
config.codexQuotaSources.enum.cacheFile: The external cache file — see tokenPace.codexQuotaFile
config.codexQuotaSources.enum.transcript: The rate_limits block Codex writes into its own transcripts — no network, no app-server, works on every platform
config.codexQuotaSources.enum.poll: Starting the local codex app-server — only with tokenPace.quotaSource set to poll
config.claudeQuotaFile.description:
JSON file holding the Claude quota state. Empty = `~/.cache/claude-usage/state.json`.

This file is written by an **external poller** (a panel plugin, a cron job, your own script), not by Claude Code itself. The format is documented in `docs/quota-cache-format.md`. Changing this path drops the cached quota state and re-reads immediately, so figures of the old identity cannot linger.
config.codexQuotaFile.description: JSON file holding the Codex quota state. Empty = `~/.cache/codex-usage/state.json`. See the note on `#tokenPace.claudeQuotaFile#`.
config.writeQuotaCache.description:
After a successful own fetch, write the result back to the cache file so other tools (panel widgets, status lines, scripts) can read the same number without a second request.

This is one of exactly **two** writes Token Pace can make outside its own extension storage, and it is off by default: enabling it asks for a separate consent that names the file. An existing file with a newer `fetched_at` is never overwritten, and the write is atomic. Format: `docs/quota-cache-format.md`.
config.codexBinary.description:
Path to the `codex` executable. Empty = `CODEX_CLI_PATH`, then `PATH`, then the binary bundled with the official IDE extension.

Machine-scoped on purpose: a workspace must not be able to point this at an arbitrary program.
config.userAgent.description:
Which `User-Agent` the quota fetch sends.

**Warning:** `honest` lands in an aggressively rate-limited bucket. Expect `429 Too Many Requests` within a few fetches, after which Token Pace backs off for up to two hours and shows nothing new. The endpoint is undocumented; this is an observation, not a documented rule.

`claudeCode` sends the same string Claude Code itself sends, with the version detected from your installed CLI (a constant if it cannot be detected).
config.userAgent.enum.claudeCode: claude-code/<version of your installed CLI> — the bucket the endpoint expects
config.userAgent.enum.honest: token-pace/<extension version> — honest, but aggressively rate limited
config.codexAppServer.mode.description: How the local `codex app-server` is used when Codex is polled. The persistent mode is killed on deactivate and restarts with a backoff.
config.codexAppServer.mode.enum.oneShot: Start codex app-server per fetch and stop it again — no long-lived child process
config.codexAppServer.mode.enum.persiste: Keep one codex app-server open and apply its rate-limit pushes directly — fresher, one more process
config.credentials.keychain.description:
Also look for the Claude access token in the OS keychain (`security` on macOS, `secret-tool` on Linux) when `~/.claude/.credentials.json` does not have it.

Only consulted while fetching is enabled and consent has been given. The token is read, used once and dropped — never cached, never logged.
config.pollOnlyWhenFocused.description: Skip scheduled fetches while the window has been in the background for more than ten minutes. A manual *Fetch Quota Now* always runs.
config.leaderElection.description:
With several VS Code windows open, let one window do the reading and fetching and have the others follow its files. Prevents duplicate requests and last-writer-wins damage to the stored history.

On any doubt (unreadable or stale lease file) a window acts as leader rather than showing nothing.
configuration.paths.title: Paths
config.claudeDir.description:
Claude Code's directory, or several of them. Empty = `~/.claude` (on Windows `%USERPROFILE%\\.claude`), or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` if that was set when VS Code started.

Accepts a string or an array of strings:

```json
"tokenPace.claudeDir": ["~/.claude", "~/work/.claude"]
```

Machine-scoped, so a synced setting cannot carry a Linux path onto a Windows machine. Takes effect after **Reload Window**.
config.codexDir.description:
Codex's directory, or several of them. Empty = `~/.codex`, or `CODEX_HOME` if that was set when VS Code started. Accepts a string or an array of strings.

Takes effect after **Reload Window**.
configuration.data.title: Data & privacy
config.hourRetentionDays.description:
How long hour-resolution buckets are kept. Older hours are merged into day buckets without losing a token — but the hour profile, the burn rate and the usage inside a running quota window need this resolution.

The compaction is irreversible.
config.retentionDays.description:
How long day buckets are kept. Older days are merged into month sums.

Note that Claude Code deletes its own transcripts after about 30 days, so anything older than that exists **only** in this snapshot and cannot be rebuilt by a re-scan.
config.quotaHistoryDays.description:
How long quota readings are kept as a time series. This is what makes burn rate, forecast, sparklines and the reset retrospective possible. `0` disables the history and those sections with it.

At `0` the `forecast` entry of `#tokenPace.statusBar.show#` and the `history` section of `#tokenPace.dashboard.sections#` have nothing left to show, and the quota cards lose their sparkline and their forecast line.
config.attribution.description:
Whether usage is attributed to projects and sessions.

With `project` or `session`, Token Pace stores **project basenames** (the last path segment of the working directory — or a salted hash, see `#tokenPace.showProjectNames#`) and **session ids** in its own extension storage. Never the full path, never a file name, and never anything from the transcript body — no prompt, no response, no tool argument and no tool result. (Tool *names* are counted for the `tools` dashboard section whatever this setting says; see the README.)

Changing this setting **triggers a full re-scan** of the transcripts, because the information is not in the existing snapshot. Switching back to `none` deletes the collected per-session records.
config.attribution.enum.none: No per-project or per-session data at all
config.attribution.enum.session: Group usage by project and by individual session
config.showProjectNames.description: How project labels appear once `#tokenPace.attribution#` is on. `hash` keeps the grouping while making the panel safe to show in a screen share.
configuration.alerts.title: Alerts
config.alerts.thresholds.description:
Percentages at which a notification is shown, e.g. `[80, 95]`.

One threshold (`90`) is set by default; **an empty list turns notifications off entirely**. Nothing here ever fires from a stale reading, at most once per window and reset cycle, and only upwards — crossing 80 % and 95 % in one step produces one message, not two.
config.alerts.basis.description: How the numbers in `#tokenPace.alerts.thresholds#` are read. Alerts stay off while that list is empty.
config.alerts.basis.enum.used: Thresholds mean “used at least this much” — 80 fires at 80 %
config.alerts.basis.enum.remaining: Thresholds mean “this much left” — 20 fires at 80 %
config.alerts.requireAhead.description:
Only alert when the window is also ahead of pace. Reaching 80 % of a weekly window on day six is not news; reaching it on day two is.

A stale reading never raises an alert; an empty `#tokenPace.alerts.thresholds#` switches notifications off entirely.
config.alerts.minRemainingMinutes.descri: Do not alert when the window resets within this many minutes — the warning would arrive too late to be worth acting on.
config.alerts.useItLoseIt.description:
Also notify about capacity that is about to expire unused (“7d window at 22 % with 9 h to go”).

Off by default, like every other alert, and never from a stale reading.
config.alerts.forecastLeadMinutes.descri:
Notify when the forecast expects the window to run out within this many minutes. `0` disables it.

Such an alert is an estimate and is labelled `~`; it needs enough readings, so it stays silent right after a reset and never fires from a stale reading.
config.alerts.onPaceFast.description:
Notify once per cycle when a window changes from on pace to ahead of pace.

Off by default; a stale reading never triggers it.
config.alerts.windowCondition.descriptio: Which windows may raise alerts at all.
config.alerts.budgetPercent.description:
Notify once per period when a budget from `#tokenPace.budgets#` passes this percentage of its own limit. `0` disables it.

One message per period and only upwards, like every other alert here. It is judged on the locally counted usage rather than on a provider reading, so it stays silent while the first read of the history is still running.
configuration.diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
config.debug.description: Verbose logging in the *Token Pace* output channel. Never logs a token, a transcript line or a response body.
config.debugLogFile.description:
Additionally write the log to this file. Empty = output channel only.

The file will contain full paths from your home directory; use *Token Pace: Copy Diagnostics* instead when you want something safe to paste into an issue.
config.diagnostics.includeNetworkSetup.d: Include the effective `http.proxy` settings and the six proxy environment variables in *Copy Diagnostics*. Credentials inside proxy URLs are replaced by `***` before anything is copied.
walkthrough.getStarted.title: Get started with Token Pace
walkthrough.getStarted.description: What the status bar is telling you, where the quota figures come from, and where the detail lives.
walkthrough.getStarted.readTheBar.title: Read the status bar
walkthrough.getStarted.readTheBar.descri:
An entry is one quota window: label, window, bar, percentage, and the countdown to its reset.

The colour compares consumption with the share of the window that has **already elapsed** — the ┃ marker in the bar. Fill left of the marker is spare, fill right of it is ahead of pace. A 60 % bar is calm an hour before the reset and loud five minutes in.

[Preview status bar states](command:tokenPace.previewStatusBar)
walkthrough.getStarted.quotaSources.desc:
Token counts are read from local transcript files. The **percentages** belong to the provider, and out of the box Token Pace only reads them from local sources somebody else already wrote — a cache file, Claude Code's own status line, **~/.claude.json**, the Codex transcripts.

"Poll" means fetching the number ourselves: one request to the provider's usage endpoint, with your access token, on the interval you set. It never happens without a dialog that says exactly what is sent where, and the answer is remembered.

[Fetch quota now](command:tokenPace.refreshQuota)
[Connect Claude status line](command:tokenPace.connectStatusLine)
[Open settings](command:tokenPace.openSettings)
walkthrough.getStarted.openDashboard.des:
The panel in the secondary sidebar carries the detail: quota cards with forecast and sustainable rate, KPIs against the previous period, per-day and per-model breakdowns, the heatmap, and a data-quality section that names every source with its age.

Where a webview is unwanted, **tokenPace.dashboard.mode** switches the same view model to a Quick Pick or a read-only markdown document.

[Open dashboard](command:tokenPace.showDashboard)
